exercises.heading: 12.3. Exercises

problem.paragraph: Which of the following expressions are meaningful? Which are meaningless? Explain.

exercises.instruction: 11–12 If $$\mathbf{u}$$ is a unit vector, find $$\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}$$ and $$\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{w}$$ .

problem.paragraph: 11. Details Three vectors are displayed. They are positioned such that they form the sides of an equilateral triangle. The first vector, labeled vector u, forms the left side, sloping down and to the left. The second vector, labeled vector v, forms the right side, sloping down and to the right. The third vector, labeled vector w, forms the horizontal base with its starting point at the tip of vector u and its tip meets the tip of vector v. $$\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = \frac{1}{2}$$ , $$\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{w} = - \frac{1}{2}$$

12. Details Three vectors are positioned along the sides and diagonals of a square. The square has a horizontal base. The first vector, labeled vector u, runs horizontally rightward along the top side of the square. The second vector, labeled vector v, runs along the diagonal connecting the top left corner to the bottom right corner until it reaches the midpoint of the diagonal. The third vector, labeled vector w, runs along the left side of the square.

A street vendor sells $$a$$ hamburgers, $$b$$ hot dogs, and $$c$$ bottles of water on a given day. He charges $$\$ 4$$ for a hamburger, $$\$ 2.50$$ for a hot dog, and $$\$ 1$$ for a bottle of water. If $$\mathbf{A} = {\langle{a,b,c}\rangle}$$ and $$\mathbf{P} = {\langle{4,2.5,1}\rangle}$$ , what is the meaning of the dot product $$\mathbf{A} \cdot \mathbf{P}$$ ?

exercises.instruction: 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, and 20 Find the angle between the vectors. (First find an exact expression and then approximate to the nearest degree.)
21–22 Find, correct to the nearest degree, the three angles of the triangle with the given vertices.
23–24 Determine whether the given vectors are orthogonal, parallel, or neither.

problem.paragraph: Use vectors to determine whether the triangle with vertices $$P\left( {1, - 3, - 2} \right)$$ , $$Q\left( {2,0, - 4} \right)$$ , and $$R\left( {6, - 2, - 5} \right)$$ is right-angled.
Find the values of $$x$$ such that the angle between the vectors $$\langle{2,1, - 1}\rangle$$ , and $$\langle{1,x,0}\rangle$$ is $$45^{{^\circ}}$$ .
Find a unit vector that is orthogonal to both $$\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}$$ and $$\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{k}$$ .
Find two unit vectors that make an angle of $$60^{{^\circ}}$$ with $$\mathbf{v} = {\langle{3,4}\rangle}$$ .

exercises.instruction: 29–30 Find the acute angle between the lines. Use degrees rounded to one decimal place.

31–32 Find the acute angles between the curves at their points of intersection. Use degrees rounded to one decimal place. (The angle between two curves is the angle between their tangent lines at the point of intersection.)
33, 34, 35, 36, and 37 Find the direction cosines and direction angles of the vector. (Give the direction angles correct to the nearest tenth of a degree.)

problem.paragraph: If a vector has direction angles $$\alpha = \pi \slash 4$$ and $$\beta = \pi \slash 3$$ , find the third direction angle $$\gamma$$ .

exercises.instruction: 39, 40, 41, 42, 43, and 44 Find the scalar and vector projections of $$\mathbf{b}$$ onto $$\mathbf{a}$$ .

problem.paragraph: Show that the vector $${orth}_{\mathbf{a}}\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{b} - {proj}_{\mathbf{a}}\mathbf{b}$$ is orthogonal to $$\mathbf{a}$$ . (It is called an orthogonal projection of $$\mathbf{b}$$ .)

For the vectors in Exercise 40, find $${orth}_{\mathbf{a}}\mathbf{b}$$ and illustrate by drawing the vectors $$\mathbf{a}$$ , $$\mathbf{b}$$ , $${proj}_{\mathbf{a}}\mathbf{b}$$ , and $${orth}_{\mathbf{a}}\mathbf{b}$$ .
If $$\mathbf{a} = {\langle{3,0, - 1}\rangle}$$ , find a vector $$\mathbf{b}$$ such that $${comp}_{\mathbf{a}}\mathbf{b} = 2$$ .

solution.paragraph: $$\langle{0,0, - 2\sqrt{10}}\rangle$$ or any vector of the form $$\langle{s,t,3s - 2\sqrt{10}}\rangle$$ , $$s$$ , $$t \in {\mathbb{R}}$$

problem.paragraph: Suppose that $$\mathbf{a}$$ and $$\mathbf{b}$$ are nonzero vectors.

Find the work done by a force $$\mathbf{F} = 8\mathbf{i} - 6\mathbf{j} + 9\mathbf{k}$$ that moves an object from the point $$\left( {0,10,8} \right)$$ along a straight line to the point $$\left( {6,12,20} \right)$$ . The distance is measured in meters and the force in newtons.

A tow truck drags a stalled car along a road. The chain makes an angle of $$30^{{^\circ}}$$ with the road and the tension in the chain is $$1500$$ N. How much work is done by the truck in pulling the car $$1$$ km?
A sled is pulled along a level path through snow by a rope. A $$30$$ -lb force acting at an angle of $$40^{{^\circ}}$$ above the horizontal moves the sled $$80$$ ft. Find the work done by the force.
A boat sails south with the help of a wind blowing in the direction $$S36^{{^\circ}}E$$ with magnitude $$400$$ lb. Find the work done by the wind as the boat moves $$120$$ ft.

Use this formula to find the distance from the point $$\left( {- 2,3} \right)$$ to the line $$3x - 4y + 5 = 0$$ .

If $$\mathbf{r} = {\langle{x,y,z}\rangle}$$ , $$\mathbf{a} = {\langle{a_{1},a_{2},a_{3}}\rangle}$$ , and $$\mathbf{b} = {\langle{b_{1},b_{2},b_{3}}\rangle}$$ , show that the vector equation $$\left( {\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{a}} \right) \cdot \left( {\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{b}} \right) = 0$$ represents a sphere, and find its center and radius.
Find the angle, in degrees rounded to one decimal place, between a diagonal of a cube and one of its edges.
Find the angle, in degrees rounded to one decimal place, between a diagonal of a cube and a diagonal of one of its faces.

A molecule of methane, $${CH}_{4}$$ , is structured with the four hydrogen atoms at the vertices of a regular tetrahedron and the carbon atom at the centroid. The bond angle is the angle formed by the $$H-C-H$$ combination; it is the angle between the lines that join the carbon atom to two of the hydrogen atoms. Show that the bond angle is about $$109.5^{{^\circ}}$$ .

[Hint: Take the vertices of the tetrahedron to be the points $$\left( {1,0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {0,1,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {0,0,1} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {1,1,1} \right)$$ , as shown in the figure. Then the centroid is $$\left( {\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}} \right)$$ .]

image.alt: Details A tetrahedron is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. Each of the vertices of the tetrahedron is labeled H. The triangular base of the tetrahedron has its vertices on the positive x, y, and z axes, while the top vertex is in the first octant. From each of the vertices, a dashed line is drawn toward the center of the tetrahedron, meeting each other at a point labeled C.

If $$\theta$$ is the angle between vectors $$\mathbf{a}$$ and $$\mathbf{b}$$ , show that

list.item: Show that if $$\mathbf{u}$$ and $$\mathbf{v}$$ are nonzero orthogonal vectors, then $$\left| {\mathbf{u} + \mathbf{v}} \right|^{2} = \left| \mathbf{u} \right|^{2} + \left. \mathbf{v} \right|^{2}$$ .

Show that the converse of part (a) is also true: if $$\left| {\mathbf{u} + \mathbf{v}} \right|^{2} = \left| \mathbf{u} \right|^{2} + \left. \mathbf{v} \right|^{2}$$ , then $$\mathbf{u}$$ and $$\mathbf{v}$$ are orthogonal.
